clue.text: Finished, with firm and yours truly getting beat

blocks.note: a match that is over is finished
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
yours truly is a jokey way of saying 'me'

explanation.surface: Someone at the end of their tether, finished with the company and feeling beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat them, so the verb is a straight synonym for winning against.

clue.text: Tolkien's goblin concealed plant

blocks.note: orcs are the goblin soldiers in The Lord of the Rings
past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A goblin from Middle-earth hid a plant somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb continuing the hiding story, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is a flowering plant family famous for its showy, exotic blooms.

clue.text: Set one's heart on cooked endive

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the word beside it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner craving a dish of cooked endive.
explanation.definitionFit: To envy something is to covet it, wanting it badly for yourself, which is setting your heart on it.

clue.text: Most attractive to arrive on foreign islet

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and altered from the familiar, so the next word gets rearranged

blocks.note: to come is to arrive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the prettiest spot is reached by landing on some little overseas island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first part on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely means pleasing to look at, so its superlative describes the best-looking of all.

clue.text: Sadly, it's ruining aim for scaling down

indicators.note: things that go sadly go wrong, so the following words are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that shrinking something spoils its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a smaller model or version of something is reducing its size, which is what scaling down means.

clue.text: Article thought to have entertained

blocks.note: the indefinite article
to muse is to ponder or think

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is reckoned to have kept readers diverted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be diverted or tickled by something, which is being entertained.

clue.text: Men look in to get fruit

indicators.note: the word before goes inside the word that precedes it

blocks.note: taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Shoppers pop into a store to buy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look in' reads as a phrasal verb meaning visit, but here the clue asks for one word placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: The melon is a large sweet fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Even, that is, for one that's a charmer

blocks.note: an even surface is a smooth one
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone pausing mid-sentence to define a charmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is informal for a suave, polished man who wins people over with easy charm.

clue.text: Day fishing, when at a loose end

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for day
angling is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: Spending a day by the river with a rod is what you do when you have nothing else on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a loose end' normally means idle; here it is taken literally, as hanging from a loose end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangling hangs freely and swings, like a rope suspended from its unfastened tip.

clue.text: Van came out to find troglodyte

indicators.note: out suggests things put out of place, so the preceding words are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A van arrived and out stepped some primitive-looking character.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is a cave-dweller, literally someone who lives in a hole in the rock.

clue.text: Everyone taking part in benefit? Swell!

indicators.note: to take part in is to be within something, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
everyone is all

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight that the whole team joined in a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell!' looks like a cheer of approval, but it is the verb meaning to expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to inflate or grow rapidly larger, which is to swell.

clue.text: Goat toys with clumsy person

blocks.note: a goat is an animal that butts
to finger something is to toy or fiddle with it

explanation.surface: A goat is playing with an awkward individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfingers is someone who keeps dropping things, as if their hands were greasy.

clue.text: Model and I do a trade

blocks.note: taken as written
to deal is to do business or trade

explanation.surface: A fashion model and the speaker strike a business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; here it means a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection to be copied, just as a model is an example worth following.

clue.text: Before giving birth in old part of South Africa, the bet was on

blocks.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker
Natal was a former province of South Africa

explanation.surface: A wager placed in colonial South Africa on a baby's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was on' sits the bet in front of the province, as a stake is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal describes the period of pregnancy and the care given to expectant mothers prior to delivery.

clue.text: Pay maturer one in distress

indicators.note: being in distress means being upset, so the letters are upset into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An older employee in difficulty needs to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like the start of 'in distress' but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is the formal word for money paid for work or services, such as salary or wages.

clue.text: O dear! More trouble for the airport

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the preceding letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller groans at yet another delay at the terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is an old-fashioned term for an airfield, a place where planes take off and land.

clue.text: Aircraft's dark shade

blocks.note: a jet is a type of aircraft
black is the darkest colour

explanation.surface: The deep colour a plane is painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet black is an intensely deep colour, named after jet, a glossy black gemstone.

clue.text: Various theorems in institution

indicators.note: various suggests many different forms, so the letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Assorted mathematical proofs taught at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institution' suggests a university after the theorems; it is a care home for the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residential establishment caring for old or infirm people, a kind of institution.

clue.text: Plug-in device with power to excite!

blocks.note: electric means powered by electricity
to fire someone up is to excite them

explanation.surface: An advert for a gadget that promises to thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: An electric fire is a mains-powered room heater, common in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: This heater runs off a wall socket, so it is a device you plug into the mains.

clue.text: Reservists strike unit on Pacific island

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
to strike is to hit
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Reserve troops launch an assault on a South Seas island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Lament lost youth, originally, with fervour

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in mourning
first letters of each word

explanation.surface: Someone mourning their vanished youth with real passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something keenly is to do it eagerly and intensely, the way fervour describes passionate zeal.

clue.text: Army unit of 10 involved in blatant trouble

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it, so one piece goes among the others
trouble throws things into disorder, so all the letters are scrambled together

blocks.note: taken as written
the figure 10 written out looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Ten soldiers from a regiment caught up in a flagrant disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not a cross-reference here: the digits 1 and 0 are read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large body of infantry, made up of several companies, within a regiment or brigade.

clue.text: Vital answer’s not recorded

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a live broadcast is not recorded

explanation.surface: An important reply was never written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital' looks like 'essential'; here it means full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital comes from the Latin for life, and something vital is living and breathing.

clue.text: Flyer for old sailor

blocks.note: first meaning: a male duck
second meaning: Sir Francis, the Elizabethan seafarer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot, a fair start for a sailor clue, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a male duck, a bird that flies, and the Elizabethan circumnavigator who fought the Armada.

clue.text: Fuss band gets from fans like this

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A pop group receives frenzied attention from its followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' plays on the pop group of the surface, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans who idolise a star show devoted love and worship, so their attitude is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Feeling energy for action

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
motion is movement or action

explanation.surface: Passion is what drives people to act.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a strong mental state such as joy or anger, which is a feeling.

clue.text: Custodian takes a look back at the Queen

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word before is read from its end

blocks.note: a peek is a quick look
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A palace guard glances over their shoulder at the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper is someone who looks after something, like a museum curator or a zoo attendant, which is a custodian.

clue.text: Sharpness as each one turned yellow, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so just the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
per means for each, as in ten pounds per person
I is the Roman numeral one
first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A tartness developed as every one of them went yellow, like fruit ripening.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity means harshness of tone or manner, a cutting edge in how something is said.
